name: banda
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Tisserant, Charles. 1930. Essai sur la grammaire banda. (Travaux et mémoires de l'Institut d'ethnologie 13.) Paris: Institut d'ethnologie. 185 pp.
catalog_locator: Phonétique, section 'ACCENT.', pp. 23-24 (Google Books scan H1cOAAAAYAAJ; =)
catalog_quote: ACCENT. La langue banda est chantée, c'est-à-dire, que chaque syllabe a sa tonalité propre, et est prononcée sur un ton plus élevé ou plus bas que la voisine. On distingue trois tons principaux: le ton haut, dans nó, dí, ká, tout, le ton moyen, dans enji, ils, le ton bas, dans mbwạnga, palabre. Nous ne noterons ici la tonalité des éléments du langage que dans la mesure où la fonction du mot dans la phrase la fait varier: ... En dehors de l'accent de hauteur, il existe en banda un accent d'intensité qui affecte certaines syllabes des mots, en sorte que les syllabes non accentuées s'abrègent et ont une tendance à disparaître: Bĕleda, tronc d'arbre, bleda; temŏ, marque du futur, tem; marœ, faire, mar.
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

new_statements.quote: La langue banda est chantée, c'est-à-dire, que chaque syllabe a sa tonalité propre, et est prononcée sur un ton plus élevé ou plus bas que la voisine. On distingue trois tons principaux : le ton haut [...], le ton moyen [...], le ton bas [...]. [...] En dehors de l'accent de hauteur, il existe en banda un accent d'intensité qui affecte certaines syllabes des mots, en sorte que les syllabes non accentuées s'abrègent et ont une tendance à disparaître : Bèleda, tronc d'arbre, bleda ; temö, marque du futur, tem ; marœ, faire, mar.
new_statements.translation: The Banda language is 'sung', that is, each syllable has its own pitch and is pronounced on a higher or lower tone than its neighbour. Three main tones are distinguished: the high tone [...], the mid tone [...], the low tone [...]. [...] Besides the pitch accent, there exists in Banda an intensity accent which affects certain syllables of words, so that the unaccented syllables are shortened and tend to disappear: Bèleda 'tree trunk', bleda; temö, future marker, tem; marœ 'to do', mar.
new_statements.citation: Tisserant, Charles. 1930. Essai sur la grammaire banda. (Travaux et mémoires de l'Institut d'ethnologie 13.) Paris: Institut d'ethnologie. 185 pp.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: the two scanned excerpts; and the full-book scanned VERBATIM: the quoted passage is on the printed pp. 23-24 under the running head PHONÉTIQUE, section heading 'ACCENT.', exactly as quoted; the bracketed ellipses correctly stand for the three tone examples (nó, dí, ká 'tout'; enji 'ils'; mbwạnga 'palabre') and the paragraph on the verbal noun raising the verb's tone. Only differences: the printed examples carry breves (Bĕleda, temŏ) which the quote renders as Bèleda, temö; 'marœ' matches. READING: agree, tone language with a stress statement. p. 23 gives three lexical tone levels; pp. 23-24 add an 'accent d'intensité' distinct from the 'accent de hauteur', identified only by the reduction/l…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Banda has three lexical tone levels (high, mid, low). Besides pitch there is an intensity (stress) accent on certain syllables of the word; syllables without it are shortened and tend to be elided (Bèleda > bleda, temö > tem, marœ > mar). The grammar does not say which syllable carries the intensity accent, and the three examples show reduction of a first syllable in one case and of a final syllable in the other two, so no positional rule can be read off.
new_statements.exceptions: None for the intensity accent. p. 24 (drum-language note) adds that loanwords receive their accents just like native Banda words ('Les mots étrangers.. reçoivent leurs accents tout comme les mots banda authentiques').
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms (Bèleda ~ bleda, temö ~ tem, marœ ~ mar). The grammar treats 'banda' as one language with dialects; Banda-Banda is explicitly one of the tribes of the main dialect (p. 4) but the accent section names no dialect, and the base variety is probably Togbo. Tone (three levels) is the primary prosody; the intensity accent is described only by its reductive effect on unaccented syllables.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Tisserant 1930) is a multidialectal 'banda' grammar whose base variety is probably Togbo (togb1241 [tor]); Banda-Banda is explicitly listed as a tribe of its main 'Dialecte banda' (p. 4) but the accent section names no dialect, and Glottolog attaches the reference to tor/bbp/lna rather than bpd. The only accessible sources that localize stress are for sister lects, not band1343: Toqué 1904 (Moruba, moru1251 under Banda-Mbrès band1342 [bqk]: initial stress in 2-3-syllable words, 1st and 3rd syllable in 4-syllable words, weak penult), Cotel 1907 (Togbo, togb1241: mostly penultimate), Sampson 1985 (Tangbago, tang1341 under Banda-Ndélé band1345 [bfl]: non-contrastive, tone-governed). The one source on a band1343 dialect proper (Blühberger 2021, Gbambiya gbam1238) is sociolinguistic and silent.

sources.citation: Sampson, Douglas L. 1985. A preliminary phonological overview of Banda-Tangbago. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 4: 133-150. (Tangbago = tang1341, under Banda-Ndélé [bfl].)
sources.note: sec. 5.2 'Stress is noncontrastive on the word level; it is governed by tone and word shape.. In two-syllable words, each syllable is stressed equally, regardless of tone. In three-syllable words, the penultimate syllable usually takes less stress than the other two, but will take more stress if it carries the only high tone in the word.' Different Banda language.

sources.citation: Toqué, Georges. 1904. Essai sur le peuple et la langue banda (région du Tchad). Paris: J. André. Avertissement p. VII: 'la tribu Banda plus particulièrement connue est la tribu Morouba.. j'ai dû prendre comme langue principale: le dialecte Morouba' = Moruba, moru1251, a dialect of Banda-Mbrès [bqk] band1342, NOT band1343.
sources.note: pp. 63-64 'ACCENT TONIQUE': 'L'accent tonique existe en langue Banda.. Règle I. Dans les mots de deux ou trois syllabes, l'accent tonique se place sur la première.. Règle II. Dans les mots de quatre syllabes, l'accent tonique se place sur la première et la troisième syllabe.. Règle III. Dans les mots simples de trois syllabes ou plus, à chaque accentuation correspond une syllabe faible, qui est la pénultième. Règle IV. Dans les mots composés, chaque mot simple est soumis aux règles précédentes.' Also 'L'absence de l'accent tonique sert à modifier la signification d'un nom' (bánga/banga, góngo…
